cl-duke-university-chatgpt-291.text: ChatGPT Edu is listed for Duke University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: institutionally licensed or procured.

evidence.quote: Duke OIT calls ChatGPT Edu an institutionally managed secure workspace. Undergraduates have unlimited access; listed faculty, staff and graduate units have no-cost access, while other community members may buy a reduced-cost licence. Setup requires Duke Software Manager, NetID@duke.edu and Duke SSO.

cl-duke-university-institutional-ai-serv.text: AI Gateway is listed for Duke University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: Duke OIT's AI Suite says AI Gateway gives Duke developers and researchers LiteLLM API keys. Its service table limits the service to developers and advanced users and describes usage-based cost recovery and a secure API.

cl-duke-university-institutional-ai-serv.text: DukeGPT is listed for Duke University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: self hosted system.

evidence.quote: Duke OIT says DukeGPT is Duke's campus-specific AI tool, hosted and managed by Duke OIT, with on-prem AI models and data kept private within Duke systems. Its comparison table lists all Duke University users and no cost for basic use.

cl-duke-university-institutional-ai-serv.text: MyGPT Builder is listed for Duke University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: Duke OIT's AI Suite describes MyGPT Builder as a secure sandboxed environment for custom AI environments. The service table limits it to university faculty, researchers and staff and states cost recovery or usage-based pricing for some models.

cl-duke-university-microsoft-copilot-295.text: Microsoft Copilot is listed for Duke University in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: allowed. Derived endorsement type: officially endorsed.

evidence.quote: Duke OIT's AI Suite says Microsoft Copilot is available at no cost to students, faculty, and staff in the university and health system, with access through Microsoft Copilot login using NetID.

claim-duke-001.text: Duke student-facing AI guidance says whether a student may use AI in coursework depends on instructor permission; unauthorized generative AI use is considered academic misconduct under the Duke Community Standard.

evidence.quote: The answer is: it depends! Per the Duke Community Standard, the unauthorized use of generative AI is considered academic misconduct. However, your instructor may permit or at times ask you to use generative AI in certain circumstances and assignments.
evidence.location: Section: Can I use AI on my Coursework?

claim-duke-002.text: Duke Community Standard academic-dishonesty guidance includes unauthorized use of artificial intelligence software among examples of cheating-related conduct.

evidence.quote: Cheating is the act of wrongfully using or attempting to use unauthorized materials, information, study aids, or the ideas or work of another. It includes, but is not limited to: using, consulting, and/or maintaining unauthorized shared resources including, but not limited to, test banks, solutions materials and/or unauthorized use of artificial intelligence (AI) software
evidence.location: Policy section: Cheating

claim-duke-003.text: Duke states that it offers a suite of secure and accessible AI platforms to students, staff, and faculty.

evidence.quote: Duke University offers a suite of secure and accessible AI platforms to students, staff, and faculty. Whether you are involved in AI research and development, or want to learn how to start using AI to power your work, Duke is here to help.
evidence.location: Section: The Duke AI Suite

claim-duke-005.text: Duke CTL guidance tells instructors to update syllabi with clear guidance on generative AI use and says instructors may define how, if, and when generative AI may be used in their courses.

evidence.quote: Under the Duke Community Standard, unauthorized use of generative AI is treated as cheating. This means you have the discretion to define how, if, and when generative AI may be used in your courses. All instructors should update their syllabi to include clear guidance on the use of generative AI in their courses.
evidence.location: Sections: Last modified note and Draft your own AI policy

claim-duke-004.text: Duke AI tool guidance describes ChatGPT as available to Duke University faculty, staff, and students, with sensitive-data use excluding PHI and governed by institutional agreement.

evidence.quote: ChatGPT is designed for a broad audience and can be used for general chatbot tasks to streamline your workflow. This includes answering questions, writing, editing, and synthesizing data and ideas. Duke University faculty, staff, and students. Prepaid licenses are provided at no cost to all undergraduate students, as well as faculty, staff, and graduate students in participating units. All other Duke users can purchase a license at a significantly discounted rate. Sensitive (no PHI), (governed by institutional agreement).
evidence.location: Table: Duke’s AI Tools: Which tool is right for me?

claim-duke-006.text: Duke CTL assignment-design guidance says AI assignments should be accompanied by course and assignment-specific AI policies, with the primary consideration being whether AI use helps students achieve course learning goals.

evidence.quote: Note, it is critical to develop AI policies for your course along with policies for specific AI assignments. In the development of AI assignments, the primary consideration is whether the use of AI will help your students achieve the learning goals of the course.
evidence.location: Sections: Generative AI Assignments and Considerations for Developing an AI Assignment

claim-duke-008.text: Duke research guidance says researchers should document and publish AI decision-making alongside research and should not cite chatbot-summarized information they have not authenticated.

evidence.quote: Do document and publish your decision-making alongside your research. Don’ts Don’t cite information found or summarized by a chatbot that you haven’t authenticated. Don’t use AI tools that collect, store, or train on user data. Check a tool’s privacy policy; if you’re not sure, contact the tool’s creator.
evidence.location: Section: Dos and Don’ts

claim-duke-007.text: Duke CTL assignment-design guidance advises that personal information should not be shared when using AI in assignments, to minimize privacy threats to students and instructors.

evidence.quote: There are ethical issues to using AI beyond questions of plagiarism, copyright and academic integrity that should be considered. First, to minimize threats to the privacy of your students and yourself, personal information should not be shared.
evidence.location: Section: Ethical Concerns
